Bachelor of Culinary Management
description:
This degree sits on top of Angliss's core reputation: the institute has trained generations of Melbourne's professional chefs, and its commercial kitchens run as genuine working production and training spaces rather than teaching-only mockups, supplying the institute's own training restaurant and bakery outlets that serve the public. Culinary Management students aren't just cooking in class; they're working alongside vocational chef apprentices and trainees in kitchens that operate under real commercial kitchen conditions and food safety obligations.

The degree is built for students aiming at kitchen leadership and food business management roles rather than a pure culinary arts (hands-on cooking) qualification. It layers business management, food cost control, and menu engineering on top of solid practical culinary skills, positioning graduates for head chef, food and beverage manager, or hospitality business owner pathways rather than line-cook roles. Angliss's placement network into Melbourne's restaurant, hotel, and catering scene (a city with a genuinely dense and competitive food industry) gives students access to kitchens ranging from high-volume hotel operations to smaller chef-driven restaurants.

Because Angliss's culinary teaching culture is built by working chefs as much as academics, expect assessment that includes live food production under time pressure and real cost-control exercises, not only written business case assignments.
curriculum:
Year 1: Culinary Fundamentals and Kitchen Operations, Food Safety and Hygiene, Introduction to Menu Planning, Hospitality Business Fundamentals, kitchen placement (short block)
Year 2: Advanced Culinary Techniques, Food and Beverage Cost Control, Menu Engineering, Kitchen Team Leadership, extended kitchen/restaurant placement
Year 3: Culinary Business Management, Supply Chain and Procurement for Food Service, Sustainable and Ethical Food Practices, Capstone Culinary Business Project, final industry placement
Practical training delivered in William Angliss's working commercial kitchens and training restaurant
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent; prior culinary certificate preferred

name: Bachelor of Event Management (Diploma to Degree Pathway)
description:
This is a stacked pathway degree: students complete a diploma-level qualification first (Angliss's diploma in event management is itself a well-regarded vocational credential in the Victorian events industry) before articulating into the bachelor's degree, which means graduates come out with both a completed diploma and a full bachelor's, a structure aimed at students who want a recognised qualification milestone partway through rather than a single long commitment.

Melbourne's genuine events economy, with major sporting events (the Australian Open, Melbourne Cup Carnival, AFL grand final), large conventions, and a dense festival calendar, gives Angliss event management students access to real, large-scale event placements that a lot of smaller event management programs elsewhere in the country simply can't offer. The diploma stage focuses heavily on operational event delivery skills (run sheets, vendor coordination, on-the-day logistics), and the degree stage builds on that with strategic event business management, marketing, and larger-scale project planning.

Because the pathway structure means students transition from a TAFE-style diploma delivery model into more strategic degree-level units partway through, the shift in workload and assessment style between the two stages is genuinely noticeable. Angliss's course advisors flag this directly to students moving between the diploma and degree components rather than treating it as a seamless continuation.
curriculum:
Diploma stage: Event Operations and Logistics, Event Marketing and Promotion, Risk Management for Events, Vendor and Stakeholder Coordination, supervised event placements
Degree stage Year 1 (post-diploma articulation): Strategic Event Management, Event Business Planning, Sponsorship and Partnership Management, Financial Management for Events
Degree stage Year 2: Large-Scale Event Project Management, Sustainable and Ethical Event Practice, Capstone Event Project (often tied to a real Melbourne event), final industry placement
Graduates receive both the diploma and bachelor's qualification through the articulated pathway
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 or equivalent; first year delivered as Diploma of Event Management

name: Bachelor of Food Studies
Bachelor of Resort and Hotel Management
description:
Angliss built this degree specifically around hotel and resort operations rather than the broader tourism-industry framing of some of its sister degrees, and the practical bent shows in the assessment style: students work through actual front office, housekeeping, and food and beverage operational scenarios using the institute's on-campus training facilities, which include a working commercial kitchen, bakery, and bar rather than only lecture-based case studies.

Placement is heavily weighted in this degree, and Angliss's long-standing relationships with major international hotel brands operating in Australia (a legacy of the institute's decades as the primary trainer for Melbourne and Victoria's hospitality workforce) mean students typically get placed into genuine hotel operations roles rather than administrative shadowing. Resort management units draw on case material from both Australian coastal and regional resort operators and international examples, reflecting graduates' genuine spread of career destinations: some go into city hotel management, others into regional or international resort operations.

Because Angliss's teaching culture leans so heavily on people who've worked the industry themselves, students should expect assessment that mirrors real operational pressure (rostering problems, service recovery scenarios, revenue management under real seasonal demand curves) rather than purely theoretical management frameworks.
curriculum:
Year 1: Hotel and Resort Operations, Front Office Management, Food and Beverage Service Operations, Customer Experience Management, industry placement (short block)
Year 2: Rooms Division Management, Resort Facilities and Recreation Management, Financial Management for Hospitality, Human Resource Management, extended industry placement
Year 3: Revenue and Yield Management, Strategic Hotel and Resort Management, Sustainable Resort Operations, Capstone Industry Project, final industry placement
Practical training delivered through William Angliss's on-campus commercial kitchen, bakery, and bar facilities

name: Bachelor of Tourism
description:
Angliss's Bachelor of Tourism leans toward destination management, tourism marketing, and sustainable tourism planning rather than the operations-heavy hospitality focus of the institute's hotel and resort degrees. It suits students aiming at roles with tourism boards, destination marketing organisations, tour operators, or the travel sector rather than on-property hotel management.

Victoria's tourism industry (Melbourne's major-events calendar, regional tourism across the Great Ocean Road and wine regions, and Victoria's state tourism agency presence) gives Angliss tourism students placement and project opportunities genuinely grounded in a real, active state tourism economy rather than abstract global tourism theory. The degree includes units on sustainable and responsible tourism, reflecting increasing industry and government focus on managing tourism's environmental and community impact, particularly relevant given Victoria's push on regional and nature-based tourism.

Because Angliss is fundamentally an industry-training institute rather than a research university, the tourism degree's teaching staff mix includes people who've worked in destination marketing organisations and tour operations, and assessment tends toward applied projects, such as actual destination marketing plans and tourism product development pitches, rather than purely theoretical tourism studies essays.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Tourism Systems, Destination Studies, Tourism Marketing Fundamentals, Customer Service in Tourism, industry placement (short block)
Year 2: Sustainable and Responsible Tourism, Tourism Product Development, Digital Marketing for Tourism, Tourism Policy and Planning, extended industry placement
Year 3: Destination Management Strategy, Tourism Business Management, Capstone Tourism Project (often tied to a real Victorian destination or operator), final industry placement
Grounded in Victoria's active tourism economy — Melbourne major events, regional and wine tourism, state tourism agency partnerships

name: Bachelor of Tourism and Hospitality Management
description:
This degree runs through the same campus that trains Angliss's chefs and baristas, which means tourism and hospitality management students aren't learning service standards purely from textbooks. The institute's commercial training restaurant, bakery, and bar operate as real, publicly trading venues, and management students do rotations through front-of-house operations there alongside the vocational trainees, giving them direct exposure to how a service business actually runs on a given shift rather than only studying it in case format.

Angliss has decades-deep relationships with Victoria's tourism and hospitality employers, and industry placement is a substantial, credit-bearing part of the degree rather than an optional add-on: students typically complete placements with hotel groups, tourism operators, or event companies across multiple points in the degree, building a genuine employment track record before graduating. The institute's location in Melbourne, a city with a real convention, major-events, and hospitality economy, gives students access to large-scale operations (major hotel chains, the Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre precinct, and a dense CBD hospitality strip) that a regional or suburban-based hospitality school couldn't match.

The degree covers both the tourism-destination-management side and hands-on hospitality operations management, and Angliss's teaching staff mix includes industry veterans as much as academics, which shows up in how practically the coursework is pitched: a lot of assessment is scenario and operations-based rather than purely essay-driven.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Tourism and Hospitality Industries, Hospitality Operations, Customer Service Management, Tourism Destination Studies, industry placement (short block)
Year 2: Rooms Division and Hotel Operations Management, Food and Beverage Management, Tourism Marketing, Human Resource Management for Hospitality, extended industry placement
Year 3: Revenue Management, Strategic Management in Tourism and Hospitality, Sustainable Tourism, Capstone Industry Project, final industry placement
Delivered with direct access to William Angliss's own training restaurant, bakery, and bar operations

Graduate Diploma of International Hotel Leadership
description:
Angliss pitches this at people already working in hotel operations who want to move into senior leadership roles without doing a full master's. It's a shorter, more intensive credential than the Master of International Hotel Leadership, aimed at hospitality professionals who need the qualification bump for a promotion or an international transfer rather than a broad career change into the industry.

The teaching draws directly on Angliss's international hotel industry connections, built over decades of the institute supplying trained staff and managers into major hotel brands across the Asia-Pacific region, and a meaningful share of each cohort is already mid-career, often studying part-time or in block-intensive mode while continuing to work in hotel operations. Coursework covers revenue management, international hotel operations standards, and leadership, with case material drawn from real branded hotel operating models rather than generic hospitality management theory.

Because the cohort skews toward working professionals, delivery is typically more flexible (block or intensive formats) than a standard academic-year degree structure, and students often complete assessments directly tied to problems from their own current workplace rather than hypothetical scenarios.
curriculum:
Core units: International Hotel Operations and Standards, Revenue and Yield Management, Leadership in Hospitality Organisations, Financial Management for Hotels
Applied units: Strategic Human Resource Management for Hotels, International Hospitality Marketing, Change Management in Hotel Operations
Capstone: Applied Leadership Project (typically addressing a real problem from the student's own workplace)
Delivered in block/intensive format to suit working hotel industry professionals

name: Master of International Hospitality Entrepreneurship
description:
William Angliss doesn't run this as an academic hospitality-theory degree. It's built for people who already have some industry background and want to launch or scale their own venture, whether that's a restaurant group, a boutique accommodation brand, or a food and beverage startup. Classes are small and run out of the institute's Melbourne CBD campus, which has its own working training restaurant, bars, and bakery on site, so the teaching staff are frequently people who've actually run venues rather than career academics, and guest lecturers tend to be working hospitality operators and investors from Melbourne's genuinely dense hospitality scene.

The degree centres on a business venture project: students develop an actual business plan or concept across the program, often one they intend to launch for real, and it gets pressure-tested against real costing, supply chain, and staffing constraints rather than treated as a hypothetical case study. Angliss's industry placement network (built over decades of supplying trained chefs, managers, and baristas to Melbourne hospitality) gives students access to venue owners and hospitality investors most standalone business schools can't offer.

Because the cohort is small and heavily practitioner-taught, the pace and flavour of each intake varies with who's enrolled and who's teaching that trimester. This isn't a large standardised MBA-style program, and Angliss is upfront that a lot of the value comes from the industry network and mentorship as much as from the coursework itself.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Hospitality Entrepreneurship Fundamentals, Financial Management for Hospitality Ventures, Market Analysis and Concept Development
Trimester 2: Supply Chain and Operations for Hospitality Businesses, Marketing and Brand Strategy, Venture Feasibility Study
Trimester 3: Leadership and People Management in Hospitality, Legal and Regulatory Frameworks for Hospitality Ventures, Business Venture Project (part 1)
Trimester 4: Investment and Growth Strategy, Business Venture Project (part 2 — capstone business plan or launched concept), industry mentorship placement
Delivered at William Angliss Melbourne campus, drawing on the institute's working training venues and hospitality industry network
admission_requirements: Successful completion of a Bachelor's degree equivalent to AQF Level 7 in a related field (Hospitality, Tourism, Culinary Arts or Hotel Management) -- not an 'any discipline' bachelor's degree as the DB states.
english_requirements: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall (or equivalent), per William Angliss Institute's published postgraduate English requirement.

name: Master of International Hotel Leadership
description:
This is Angliss's senior credential for hotel industry professionals, longer and more research-oriented than the Graduate Diploma of International Hotel Leadership, and it's pitched at people aiming for general manager or regional leadership roles within international hotel brands rather than a first entry into hospitality management. The program draws on Angliss's genuinely deep international hotel industry relationships, built over decades of training staff who go on to work across branded hotel groups throughout the Asia-Pacific region.

Coursework moves from operational hotel leadership topics into higher-level strategic and international business content: cross-cultural management, international hotel branding and franchise models, and hospitality investment and asset management, reflecting the reality that senior hotel leaders increasingly need to understand ownership and brand-management structures, not just day-to-day operations. The capstone research or applied project typically has students examining a real strategic problem in international hotel operations, often connected to their own employer or a target market.

Given the practitioner-heavy cohort (most students are already working in hotel management), Angliss runs the degree with flexible block and intensive delivery options, and it's common for students to be sponsored or part-supported by their current employer as part of a leadership development plan, which shapes both the applied focus of assessments and the seniority of typical classroom discussion.
curriculum:
Core units: International Hotel Leadership and Strategy, Cross-Cultural Management in Hospitality, Hotel Branding and Franchise Models, Financial and Asset Management for Hotels
Advanced units: Hospitality Investment and Development, Global Hotel Operations Standards, Strategic Human Resource Leadership
Capstone: Applied Research Project or Strategic Business Project (often connected to the student's own employer or target market)
Delivered in block/intensive format for working international hotel industry professionals
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree or equivalent, hospitality industry experience preferred
